title: CABG indications and guidelines: left main stenosis, multivessel CAD, trial evidence and medical therapy
subject: ss-ctvs

2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Guideline for Coronary Artery Revascularization

steps.say: Surgical revascularization provides an established survival advantage in significant left main coronary artery disease. When luminal diameter stenosis exceeds fifty percent, bypass grafting outperforms percutaneous intervention in long-term mortality and repeat intervention rates. This benefit holds robustly across diverse clinical subsets.
steps.tx: Coronary artery bypass grafting confers a decisive long-term **survival advantage** over **percutaneous coronary intervention** in patients harboring significant **left main coronary stenosis** exceeding 50 percent. Bypassing the left main bifurcation protects the entire anterior and circumflex territories against catastrophic occlusion.

steps.say: In patients with three-vessel disease, anatomical complexity dictates the revascularization strategy. When the SYNTAX score is greater than twenty-two, surgical bypass achieves superior outcomes compared with stents. Patients experience significantly fewer major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events on long-term follow-up.
steps.tx: Surgical grafting is strongly preferred for **three-vessel disease** characterized by intermediate-to-high anatomical complexity, defined by an angiographic **SYNTAX score** greater than 22. In this patient cohort, bypass achieves significantly lower long-term **MACCE** rates and prevents recurrent spontaneous infarction compared to percutaneous stenting.

rows: PCI or CABG equivalent in low-risk subsets
CABG strongly recommended; clear survival superiority

steps.say: Diabetes mellitus amplifies the benefits of coronary bypass surgery. Landmark findings from the FREEDOM trial proved that bypass surgery confers superior five-year survival over drug-eluting stents in diabetic multivessel disease. Patients also suffer significantly fewer repeat myocardial infarctions when treated surgically.
steps.tx: In patients with **diabetes mellitus** and complex multivessel disease, the landmark **FREEDOM trial** established that surgical revascularization provides superior 5-year all-cause survival and significantly lower repeat infarction rates compared with **drug-eluting stents**. Diffuse microvascular diabetic vasculopathy benefits substantially from durable surgical bypass conduits.

left.title: FREEDOM Trial: CABG Arm
points: Marked reduction in recurrent myocardial infarction

right.title: FREEDOM Trial: PCI Arm
points: Higher repeat intervention and target lesion failure
Higher 5-year death and recurrent infarction rates
Slight early reduction in perioperative stroke

steps.say: Severe ischemic cardiomyopathy also benefits profoundly from surgical bypass. The STICH trial demonstrated that patients with an ejection fraction of thirty-five percent or lower achieve improved ten-year survival with surgery plus medical therapy compared to medical management alone. This survival gain reflects ischemic protection and reverse remodeling.
steps.tx: For patients suffering from **ischemic cardiomyopathy** with severe ventricular systolic dysfunction, defined by a **left ventricular ejection fraction** of 35 percent or lower, the landmark **STICH trial** demonstrated that surgical bypass combined with guideline medical therapy delivers superior 10-year all-cause survival over medical therapy alone.

nodes.label: CAD with LVEF <= 35% on optimal medical therapy
Perform viability and coronary anatomy assessment
Perform CABG plus full guideline medical therapy
Achieve superior 10-year survival and reverse remodeling

steps.say: Aim for complete anatomical revascularization during the operation. Graft every major coronary artery that is one point five millimetres or larger with at least fifty percent narrowing. Incomplete grafting leaves ischemic territories behind, increasing future repeat revascularization and recurrent angina.
steps.tx: Achieving **complete revascularization** by grafting every major ischemic coronary bed with a **vessel caliber** of 1.5 mm or greater and luminal stenosis of 50 percent or greater is critical. Complete anatomical coverage minimizes residual ischemia, shields unbypassed myocardium, and markedly reduces late **ischemic events** and repeat reinterventions.

left.title: Complete Revascularization
points: Grafts all vessels >= 1.5 mm with >= 50% stenosis
Reduced risk of angina recurrence and reintervention

right.title: Incomplete Revascularization
points: Elevated risk of repeat catheter revascularization

steps.say: Complex revascularization decisions demand formal multidisciplinary consultation. Guidelines designate the Heart Team approach as a Class I recommendation for guiding therapy in complex multivessel disease. Cardiac surgeons and interventionalists jointly evaluate surgical risk, coronary anatomy, and patient comorbidities.
steps.tx: Guideline authorities assign a **Class I recommendation** to the multidisciplinary **Heart Team** approach, comprising a cardiac surgeon, interventional cardiologist, and clinical cardiologist. This collaborative forum makes an individualized **multidisciplinary decision**, balancing procedural mortality risks, anatomical complexity, and patient preferences to select optimal revascularization.

rows: STS score and EuroSCORE II predicted mortality
SYNTAX score and chronic total occlusion feasibility
Cognitive status, functional independence, life expectancy

steps.say: Emergency surgery is required for specific mechanical catastrophes and refractory acute ischemia. In ST-elevation myocardial infarction, emergency bypass rescues patients with failed percutaneous intervention, ongoing shock, or acute mechanical complications such as ventricular septal rupture and papillary muscle tear.
steps.tx: During acute **ST-elevation myocardial infarction**, emergency surgical bypass is urgently indicated for persistent refractory ischemia, **failed PCI** accompanied by hemodynamic instability, or acute **mechanical complications** such as ventricular septal rupture or ischemic papillary muscle disruption requiring simultaneous emergency surgical repair under cardiopulmonary bypass.

nodes.label: Acute STEMI with shock or acute mechanical complication
Transfer immediately to cardiac surgical operating theater
Emergency CABG with concomitant mechanical lesion repair

steps.say: Aggressive secondary prevention must begin promptly after surgery. Prescribe dual antiplatelet therapy and high-intensity statin therapy to protect saphenous vein conduits against acute thrombosis. Long-term medical compliance preserves conduit patency and retards native plaque progression.
steps.tx: Postoperative secondary medical prevention mandates **dual antiplatelet therapy** and **high-intensity statin** administration. Antiplatelet inhibition suppresses early **vein graft thrombosis**, while intensive statin therapy halts endothelial atheroma progression, preserving long-term conduit patency and conferring sustained patient survival across diverse clinical subsets.
